To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) ferrates (Fe VI) are efficient oxidants for PAH degradation in DNAPL contaminated soil; (2) they produce less oxygenated by-products than permanganate and Fenton-like; (3) their auto-decomposition leads to lower degradation yields; (4) the degradation efficiency is not significantly affected by the presence of the dense non aqueous liquid phase.
ferrateVI oxidation is an efficient process to degrade a wide range of polycyclic compounds (both PAHs and PACs) in soils and can be considered as an interesting option for remediation.
